title.narrative: ''Climate Smart Agricultural Research and Innovation Support for Dairy Value Chains in Eritrea''

description.narrative: The project addresses an inclusive, sustainable and climate relevant transformation of the Eritrean dairy value chain to enhance food and nutrition security, reduce poverty and create job opportunities for young people. In line with the main themes of DeSIRA, the action is designed to accelerate access to innovation in the Eritrean dairy sector, encompassing the development and transfer of technologies for primary milk production, for all stages of dairy processing.

Given the difficulty of measuring income change in a robust manner, given the challenge of linking income change to agriculture only, and given that income indicators at project level are often attached to different definitions, measurement methods and units, this indicator is proposed with the assumption that projects planning to report on income change can also report on the number of farmers whose income has increased. A farmer whose perception that farming income has increased would be counted under this indicator, even in the absence of a formal assessment of the income change.The claim that farming income has increased should result from taking up innovative (or new) techniques, practices, systems, products, services or knowledge introduced by the DeSIRA project. Primary interventions that incorporate this indicator in their logframe are likely to conduct a specific survey to measure this indicator.

The definition excludes small industrial firms processing food.Coping is a broad term that means dealing effectively with something difficult. Being equipped to cope with climate change (CC) related shocks encompasses a diversity of mitigation, anticipation or adaptation strategies and skills, and may differ from one project to another. The claim/feeling that a farmer is better equipped to cope with CC should result from this farmer taking up (or applying) innovative (or new) techniques, practices, systems, products, services or knowledge introduced by the DeSIRA project. However, this indicator is not equivalent to another result indicator, the number of farmers who have taken up innovations, which is strictly quantitative . In comparison, thsi indicator has a strong qualitative dimension. It reflects the perception of farmers visvis innovations introduced by the intervention and a change of behaviour visvis climaterelated shocks, due to increased capacity. Primary interventions that incorporate this indicator in their logframe are likely to conduct a specific survey to measure this indicator.
